title: ML Numerics and Loss Curves
prompt:
Implement four numerical utilities. `stable_softmax(logits)` normalizes the final axis without overflow. `standardize_columns(X)` standardizes each feature and rejects a constant column. `ridge_gradient(X, y, weights, bias, l2)` returns gradients for mean squared error plus `l2 * ||weights||²`; regularization applies to weights, not the bias. `LossCurve(values)` supports `moving_average(window)` and `best_window(window)`, returning the earliest start index of the smallest moving average. Reject nonpositive or oversized windows.

Use vectorized NumPy operations; the loss-curve methods should be linear in the number of recorded values.

example.reasoning: The windows at indices 1 and 2 tie, so the earlier one wins.
